en: The Chapter on Similes, Section on the Monkey.
1. The Question on the Spider’s Limb “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘one limb of the spider should be adopted,’ which is that one limb that should be adopted?
“Just as, Great King, a spider makes a web of threads across a path, and if a worm, a fly, or a moth becomes caught there in that web, it seizes it and eats it;”
In the same way, Great King, a yogin practicing yoga, having spread the canopy of the net of mindfulness over the six sense-doors, must kill right there any flies of defilement that become caught.
This, Great King, is one quality to be taken from the road-monkey.
And this, Great King, was said by the Elder Anuruddha:
“Restrain the mind at the six sense-doors with the supreme foundation of mindfulness;
if defilements should cling there, [then apply the appropriate remedy].”
Thus ends the first question concerning the monkey on the path.
